title: Climb the stairs
brief:
Karel must climb three steps and pick up the beeper at the top.

Karel has no turn_right() command. Write one yourself: a function called turn_right() that turns left three times.

Then write a second function, climb_step(), that climbs exactly one step: turn left, move up, turn right, move forward. Use it three times in main(). Breaking a job into small named pieces is called decomposition.

vocabulary.gloss: the keyword that creates a new function
a small function you write to do one job, so main() stays short and readable
breaking a big problem into smaller problems and solving each one
a line that does nothing. It keeps a function valid while it is still empty — replace it with real commands

hints: Inside turn_right(), write turn_left() three times. Inside climb_step(), write: turn_left(), move(), turn_right(), move() — you can call your own turn_right() there.
In main(), call climb_step() three times, then pick_beeper().
If Karel walks into a wall, run it at slow speed and watch which step goes wrong. Each function body must be indented by 4 spaces.
solution:
def turn_right():
    turn_left()
    turn_left()
    turn_left()

def climb_step():
    turn_left()
    move()
    turn_right()
    move()

def main():
    climb_step()
    climb_step()
    climb_step()
    pick_beeper()
